**Best next move:** with the first weekly inspo, keep her great "you've got your hands full" hook but flip the payoff to arm and back relief, and ask her to film with her one year old actually in the sling.

### Style (from watching her videos)
- On camera: mom with long wavy light-brown hair, white crochet bandana, chambray dress, very relaxed and conversational. No child appears in her video (she talks about her one year old). Setting: a plain bedroom with a ceiling fan and white doors. Checkered sling.
- Format: talking head with small burned-in word captions, 32 seconds. Opens with the text quote "you've got your hands full". She demos the sling empty: shows the padded strap, puts it over her head, adjusts, folds it small "so I can keep it in my purse or in my car". Signature phrase: "I have no notes."
- Script: "As a mom of three under five, people try to tell me that my hands are always full, but that actually isn't true anymore because I got the Bambora Sling Carrier and my hands are completely free. My one-year-old just likes to sit right here on the hip."
- What worked: 46285b10 (Aug 22, re-uploaded with better volume) approved and running: $260 spend, 4 purchases, $225. Below break even.
- Safety and checklist: no baby in the video, so the one-hand and seat checks do not apply; but the whole hook is the retired hands-free claim, and it is running in an ad. Burned-in captions (checklist 6).
- Strengths: strong relatable hook (the stranger's "you've got your hands full" comment), natural delivery, compact and purse-friendly angle.
- To improve: show the sling on her one year old (seat under bottom, one hand on); reframe the payoff as "my arms finally get a break".
